narrative.northStar: From the same hand as the mark
narrative.overview:
Freehand's native Avalonia interface looks like it came from the same hand as its logo: a soft cream cursive f on warm black. The window is the logo's black, raised surfaces are a half-step warmer, and one cream accent carries every selection, primary action, toggle, and focus. Controls are soft pills. The f mark sits at the left of the header, and a filled swash cut from the f's crossbar sits under the selected tab. Windows keeps its title bar and window controls, and the application requests the dark Fluent theme.

The layout carries the meaning, so the copy stays short. There are no page titles, counts, entry-type labels, or helper lines. Search opens each tab, with that tab's actions beside it, and transcript text takes the remaining space. Red still means recording and amber still means attention.

History. Sam selected the Compact structure on October 22, 2026. The approved [decision image](.impeccable/mocks/decision/compact.png) and [browser prototype](src/Freehand.App/Prototypes/Compact/index.html) record that approval; the prototype remains a throwaway interaction study. On November 19, 2026, Sam approved a retheme of that structure toward the logo ("Retheme + cut copy", "Cream from the logo"), which replaced the graphite and sage palette, the waveform and wordmark, and the page headings. Code classes keep the Compact name (`CompactTheme`, `compact-*` captures). The cassette and field-recorder appearance remains the confirmed anti-reference.

This file describes the implemented native system. Apply these values through [DesignTokens.cs](src/Freehand.App/Design/DesignTokens.cs) and [CompactTheme.cs](src/Freehand.App/Design/CompactTheme.cs). Code owns rendering; keep this specification and [.impeccable/design.json](.impeccable/design.json) in sync with it. Earlier native evidence and adaptations are recorded in [compact-native.md](docs/design/compact-native.md); retheme captures are in `.impeccable/review/logo/`.
keyCharacteristics: Warm black ground with warm cream ink; no cool grays.
One cream accent, used for selection, primary actions, toggles, focus, and the swash.
The f mark is the only brand element; there is no wordmark.
No page titles or filler copy; search is the first row.

rules.name: The One Cream Rule
rules.body: Cream is the only accent. Anything chosen, primary, or focused is cream; everything else is warm black, warm panel, ink, or muted.

rules.name: The Status Pair Rule
rules.body: Red and amber appear only as state, always paired with text and, where one exists, an action. Attention feedback in the main window has a one-DIP amber border and amber message; ordinary transcript availability has no border.

rules.name: The No Filler Rule
rules.body: Use sentence case and keep text that names a control, reports a state, or explains a recovery action. Cut page titles, counts, entry-type labels, taglines, and helper lines that repeat what the layout shows.

rules.name: The Crossbar Rule
rules.body: The swash marks the selected tab and nothing else. It is filled, not stroked, and never becomes a generic underline.

dos: Do keep routine dictation in the tray and preserve the receiving app's focus.
Do use native tokens and Fluent controls when adding or changing a view.
Do use cream for every selected, primary, or focused state, and nothing else.
Do pair red recording and amber attention with explicit text.
Do preserve real history, dictionary, settings, and recovery behavior.
donts: Don't add page titles, counts, type labels, taglines, or helper lines.
Don't add a wordmark or a second brand mark beside the f.
Don't reintroduce graphite, sage, or other cool neutrals.
Don't add recorder textures, bevels, decorative labels, or browser demo controls.
Don't treat a headless capture as hardware validation, installation, or publication.
